title: Structural Biology
tagline: Protein architecture and folding, nucleic acids, X-ray crystallography, NMR, cryo-EM, structure prediction, molecular machines and dynamics
summary: Structural biology explains how biological molecules work by locating their atoms. This course covers the architecture and folding of proteins and nucleic acids, the methods that determine structures — X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy and cryo-electron microscopy — the prediction of structure from sequence, and what structures reveal about molecular machines, dynamics and binding.

chapters.title: Protein architecture
chapters.summary: Secondary structure, folds, domains and the classification of protein structures.

chapters.title: Protein folding and stability
chapters.summary: The energy landscape of folding, chaperones, misfolding and aggregation.

chapters.title: Structures of nucleic acids
chapters.summary: Forms of DNA, RNA folding and ribozymes, and how proteins recognise DNA and RNA.

chapters.title: X-ray crystallography
chapters.summary: Crystals, diffraction, the phase problem and building a model into an electron-density map.

chapters.title: NMR and spectroscopic methods
chapters.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance of proteins, and circular dichroism and fluorescence for structure and dynamics.

chapters.title: Cryo-electron microscopy
chapters.summary: Single-particle analysis, electron tomography and the resolution revolution.

chapters.title: Predicting structure
chapters.summary: Homology modelling, physics-based methods and deep-learning prediction from AlphaFold onwards.

chapters.title: Molecular machines
chapters.summary: How structures explain function: the ribosome, ATP synthase, motor proteins and membrane transporters.

chapters.title: Dynamics, binding and design
chapters.summary: Conformational change, ligand binding, molecular dynamics simulation and the design of new proteins.
